source.title: 50 Stories of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ and His Companions
source.note: Written from general knowledge of the classical sources, without live access to them. Names, numbers and attributions should be checked before teaching or publishing.

parts.title: Character, Mercy and the Lives of the Companions

stories.title: The First Revelation in the Cave of Hira
paras: At about forty years of age, the Prophet ﷺ used to retreat to the Cave of Hira on Jabal al-Nur to worship. There the angel Jibril came to him and commanded, "Read!" He replied, "I am not a reader." After the angel pressed him three times, the first verses of Surah al-Alaq were revealed. He returned home trembling and said to Khadijah, "Cover me, cover me."

Khadijah comforted him, saying Allah would never disgrace him because he kept family ties, helped the weak, honoured guests and supported people in hardship. She took him to her cousin Waraqah ibn Nawfal, a Christian scholar, who recognised the signs of prophethood and said his people would drive him out.

head: p
khadijah-bint-khuwaylid
lines.role: his wife; comforted him, affirmed his character, and became the first person to believe in him.

head: p
waraqah-ibn-nawfal
lines.role: Khadijah's cousin who confirmed the revelation; he died soon after, and many scholars count him among the believers.

head: p
aishah-bint-abi-bakr
lines.role: the main narrator of this hadith in Sahih al-Bukhari, as she heard it from the Prophet ﷺ.

stories.title: The First Believers
paras: After Khadijah, the first to accept Islam were Ali ibn Abi Talib, a boy living in the Prophet's household, Zayd ibn Harithah, his freed servant and adopted son, and Abu Bakr, his closest friend, who believed without hesitation. Abu Bakr then invited his own friends, and five of the ten promised Paradise entered Islam through him.

head: p
khadijah-bint-khuwaylid
lines.role: first of all believers.

head: p
abu-bakr-al-siddiq

head: p
ali-ibn-abi-talib

zayd-ibn-harithah

stories.title: The Call from Mount Safa
paras: When Allah revealed "And warn your nearest kin" (26:214), the Prophet ﷺ climbed Mount Safa and called each clan of Quraysh by name. He asked, "If I told you an army was behind this hill, would you believe me?" They said, "We have never known you to lie." He said, "Then I am a warner to you of a severe punishment." His uncle Abu Lahab cursed him, and Surah al-Masad was revealed in reply.

abdullah-ibn-abbas
lines.role: narrator of the hadith in al-Bukhari and Muslim.

head: p
ali-ibn-abi-talib
lines.role: present at the related gathering of Banu Abd al-Muttalib, where he alone stood up in support of the Prophet ﷺ.

stories.title: Bilal and "Ahad, Ahad"
paras: Bilal was enslaved by Umayyah ibn Khalaf, who laid him on burning sand at midday with a heavy rock on his chest, demanding he reject Islam. Bilal only repeated, "Ahad, Ahad" (One, One). Abu Bakr bought him and set him free, and went on to free several other tortured believers.

head: p
bilal-ibn-rabah
lines.role: endured the torture; later the first mu'adhdhin of Islam.

head: p
abu-bakr-al-siddiq

amir-ibn-fuhayrah

head: p
zinnirah-al-rumiyyah

stories.title: The Family of Yasir
paras: Yasir, his wife Sumayyah and their son Ammar were tortured by Banu Makhzum under Abu Jahl. Passing by, the Prophet ﷺ said, "Patience, O family of Yasir, your promised meeting place is Paradise." Abu Jahl killed Sumayyah with a spear, making her the first martyr of Islam; Yasir also died under torture. When Ammar was forced to say words of disbelief, Allah revealed that one compelled while his heart is firm in faith is excused (16:106).

head: p
sumayyah-bint-khayyat
lines.role: first martyr in Islam.

head: p
yasir-ibn-amir
lines.role: martyred under torture.

head: p
ammar-ibn-yasir
lines.role: survived; the verse of compulsion was revealed about him.

stories.title: Abdullah ibn Mas'ud Recites at the Ka'bah
paras: The Companions wanted someone to recite the Qur'an aloud to Quraysh. Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, a small man with no powerful clan, volunteered. He stood at the Maqam and recited Surah al-Rahman until Quraysh beat him. He returned bruised and said he was ready to do it again the next day.

head: p
abdullah-ibn-masud
lines.role: first to recite the Qur'an publicly in Makkah after the Prophet ﷺ.
The early Companions gathered with him, who warned him he had no clan to protect him.

stories.title: Hamzah Accepts Islam
paras: Abu Jahl insulted and harmed the Prophet ﷺ near Safa. When Hamzah returned from hunting, a freedwoman told him what had happened. Furious, he went to Abu Jahl at the Ka'bah, struck him with his bow, and declared, "Will you insult him when I follow his religion?" He then embraced Islam fully, and Quraysh became more cautious.

head: p
hamzah-ibn-abd-al-muttalib
lines.role: the Prophet's uncle; "Lion of Allah."

stories.title: Umar ibn al-Khattab Accepts Islam
paras: Umar set out with his sword to kill the Prophet ﷺ. Nu'aym ibn Abdullah told him his own sister had become Muslim. Umar burst into her house, where Khabbab was teaching her and her husband Surah Ta-Ha, and struck her. Seeing her blood and steadfastness, he asked to read the page. Moved, he went to Dar al-Arqam and accepted Islam. The Prophet ﷺ had prayed, "O Allah, strengthen Islam with one of the two Umars." After this, Muslims prayed openly at the Ka'bah.

head: p
umar-ibn-al-khattab
lines.role: accepted Islam; later called al-Faruq.

head: p
fatimah-bint-al-khattab
lines.role: his sister, whose firmness moved him.

head: p
said-ibn-zayd

head: p
khabbab-ibn-al-aratt

head: p
nuaym-ibn-abdullah-al-nahham

head: p
al-arqam-ibn-abi-al-arqam
lines.role: owner of the house where the Muslims met.

head: p
hamzah-ibn-abd-al-muttalib
lines.role: stood guard at the door when Umar arrived.

stories.title: Ja'far Before the Negus of Abyssinia
paras: To escape persecution, a group of Muslims migrated to Abyssinia under a just Christian king. Quraysh sent Amr ibn al-As and Abdullah ibn Abi Rabi'ah with gifts to bring them back. Ja'far ibn Abi Talib spoke for the Muslims, describing the ignorance they had left and the truth they had found, then recited from Surah Maryam. The Negus wept and refused to hand them over.

stories.title: The Boycott in Shi'b Abi Talib
paras: Quraysh hung a pact in the Ka'bah to boycott Banu Hashim and Banu al-Muttalib: no trade, no marriage. For about three years the Prophet ﷺ and his family were confined to a valley, surviving on leaves and scraps. Some sympathetic Qurayshis worked to end it, and the document was found eaten by termites except for the words "In Your name, O Allah," just as the Prophet ﷺ had said.

head: p
khadijah-bint-khuwaylid

stories.title: The Journey to Ta'if
paras: After the deaths of Abu Talib and Khadijah in the Year of Sorrow, the Prophet ﷺ walked to Ta'if to invite Thaqif. Its leaders rejected him and set youths to stone him until his feet bled. Resting in a garden, he made his famous supplication. The angel of the mountains offered to crush the town, but he said, "I hope Allah will bring from their descendants people who worship Him alone." A Christian servant named Addas brought him grapes and believed.

head: p
zayd-ibn-harithah
lines.role: accompanied him and shielded him from the stones, suffering head wounds.

head: p
addas
lines.role: the servant from Nineveh who believed in him.

head: p
aishah-bint-abi-bakr

stories.title: Al-Isra wal-Mi'raj
paras: In one night the Prophet ﷺ was taken from Makkah to Jerusalem, where he led the prophets in prayer, then ascended through the heavens, where the five daily prayers were prescribed. When he told Quraysh, they mocked him and ran to Abu Bakr. Abu Bakr said, "If he said it, it is true," earning the title al-Siddiq.

head: p
abu-bakr-al-siddiq
lines.role: affirmed the journey immediately.

head: p
umm-hani-bint-abi-talib

stories.title: The Pledges of Aqabah
paras: In the pilgrimage seasons, groups from Yathrib met the Prophet ﷺ at Aqabah. Twelve pledged in the first year, and he sent Mus'ab ibn Umayr back with them as teacher. Through Mus'ab, the chiefs Sa'd ibn Mu'adh and Usayd ibn Hudayr accepted Islam. The next year seventy-three men and two women pledged to protect him as they would their own families, opening the way to the Hijrah.

stories.title: The Hijrah and the Cave of Thawr
paras: Quraysh plotted to kill the Prophet ﷺ in his bed. Ali slept in his place under his green cloak, and the Prophet ﷺ left with Abu Bakr for the Cave of Thawr. When the trackers stood at its mouth, Abu Bakr whispered his fear, and the Prophet ﷺ said, "What do you think of two when Allah is the third?" (9:40). After three days they set out for Madinah. Suraqah ibn Malik chased them for the bounty, but his horse's legs sank into the sand three times; he asked for safety and was promised the bracelets of Kisra.

head: p
abu-bakr-al-siddiq

head: p

stories.note: Abdullah ibn Urayqit, their hired guide, was not a Muslim at the time.

stories.title: Arrival in Madinah and the Building of the Mosque
paras: The people of Madinah went out every morning to wait for the Prophet ﷺ. When he arrived, children sang, and every family wanted to host him. He let his camel walk freely, saying "She is commanded." She knelt by a plot owned by two orphans, and he stayed at the nearby house of Abu Ayyub. The land was bought, and the Prophet ﷺ carried bricks alongside his Companions to build the mosque.

stories.title: The Brotherhood of the Muhajirun and Ansar
paras: The Prophet ﷺ paired each emigrant from Makkah with a helper from Madinah as brothers. Sa'd ibn al-Rabi' offered Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf half his wealth. Abd al-Rahman thanked him and said, "Just show me the way to the market." He traded and soon prospered.

stories.title: Salman al-Farisi's Search for Truth
paras: Salman was born a Zoroastrian in Persia. Drawn to Christianity, he served a series of monks; the last told him a prophet would appear in a land of palms, who would accept gifts but not charity and carry the seal of prophethood between his shoulders. Sold into slavery in Madinah, he tested the Prophet ﷺ on all three signs and accepted Islam. The Prophet ﷺ helped him buy his freedom by planting 300 palm saplings with his own hands.

lines.role: the seeker.

The Companions who planted the palms with the Prophet ﷺ, and those who contributed gold for his ransom.

stories.title: The First Adhan
paras: The Muslims discussed how to gather people for prayer: a bell, a horn or a fire. Abdullah ibn Zayd saw the words of the adhan in a dream. The Prophet ﷺ said, "It is a true vision. Teach it to Bilal, for his voice is stronger." When Umar heard Bilal, he ran out saying he had seen the same dream.

stories.title: Abdullah ibn Salam Accepts Islam
paras: Abdullah ibn Salam, a leading Jewish scholar of Madinah, asked the Prophet ﷺ three questions only a prophet would know, and was satisfied. Before announcing his Islam, he hid while the Prophet ﷺ asked his community about him. They called him their best and son of their best. When he came out and declared his faith, they called him their worst.

head: p
abdullah-ibn-salam
lines.role: the scholar who believed; the Prophet ﷺ gave him glad tidings of Paradise.

head: p

head: p
khalidah-bint-al-harith

stories.title: The Battle of Badr
paras: In Ramadan of 2 AH, 313 Muslims with two horses faced about 1,000 Quraysh. Before battle, the Prophet ﷺ consulted his Companions, and both Muhajirun and Ansar pledged to follow him even into the sea. He spent the night in supplication until his cloak fell from his shoulders. Allah sent angels in support, and Quraysh were defeated, losing seventy dead including Abu Jahl.

stories.title: The Battle of Uhud
paras: In 3 AH, Quraysh returned with 3,000 men. The Prophet ﷺ placed fifty archers on a hill with orders never to leave. When the Muslims began winning, most archers left for the spoils. Khalid ibn al-Walid circled behind, and the Muslims were thrown into confusion. A rumour spread that the Prophet ﷺ had been killed. He was wounded in the face and his tooth broken, while a small band of Companions shielded him.

stories.title: Anas ibn al-Nadr: "I Smell Paradise"
paras: Anas ibn al-Nadr missed Badr and vowed that if Allah let him witness another battle, Allah would see what he would do. At Uhud, when others wavered, he said to Sa'd ibn Mu'adh, "Paradise! By the Lord of the Ka'bah, I smell its scent beyond Uhud." He was found with more than eighty wounds, recognised only by his sister from his fingertips. The verse "Among the believers are men who were true to their covenant with Allah" (33:23) is linked to him.

head: p
anas-ibn-al-nadr
lines.role: the martyr.

head: p
sad-ibn-muadh
lines.role: whom he addressed; Sa'd said, "I could not do what he did."

head: p
al-rubayyi-bint-al-nadr

head: p
anas-ibn-malik
lines.role: his nephew, narrator of the story.

stories.title: The Battle of the Trench (al-Khandaq)
paras: In 5 AH, about 10,000 confederates marched on Madinah. On Salman's advice, the Muslims dug a trench across the open northern side in freezing cold and hunger. When a rock defeated them, the Prophet ﷺ struck it three times, and with each spark foretold the conquest of Syria, Persia and Yemen. After nearly a month, discord among the enemy and a fierce wind broke the siege.

head: p
salman-al-farisi
lines.role: proposed the trench; the Prophet ﷺ said, "Salman is one of us, the People of the House."

head: p
jabir-ibn-abdullah
t
and his wife
p
suhaylah-bint-masud
lines.role: prepared a small goat and some barley that, by the Prophet's blessing, fed the whole army.

head: p
ali-ibn-abi-talib
lines.role: answered the challenge of the champion Amr ibn Abd Wudd and killed him.

head: p
nuaym-ibn-masud
lines.role: a new Muslim who sowed distrust between Quraysh and Banu Qurayzah.

head: p
hudhayfah-ibn-al-yaman
lines.role: crossed into the enemy camp on the coldest night to bring news.

head: p
al-zubayr-ibn-al-awwam
lines.role: volunteered to scout; the Prophet ﷺ called him "my disciple (hawari)."

head: p
sad-ibn-muadh
lines.role: struck by an arrow in his arm (see story 24).

head: p
safiyyah-bint-abd-al-muttalib
lines.role: defended the women's fort against an enemy who approached it.

head: p
hassan-ibn-thabit

head: p
al-bara-ibn-azib
lines.role: narrated the Prophet ﷺ carrying earth until dust covered his chest.

head: p

khalid-ibn-al-walid

ikrimah-ibn-abi-jahl
lines.role: among the confederates (all accepted Islam later).

stories.title: The Death of Sa'd ibn Mu'adh
paras: Wounded at the Trench, Sa'd prayed that he would not die until his heart was at peace regarding Banu Qurayzah, who had broken their treaty in the Muslims' most dangerous hour. Their case was referred to his judgment, which the Prophet ﷺ said matched the judgment of Allah. His wound then reopened and he died. The Prophet ﷺ said, "The Throne of the Most Merciful shook at the death of Sa'd ibn Mu'adh," and seventy thousand angels attended his funeral.

head: p
sad-ibn-muadh
lines.role: chief of Aws.

head: p
rufaydah-al-aslamiyyah
lines.role: nursed him in her tent in the mosque, the first field hospital in Islam.

head: p
abu-lubabah-ibn-abd-al-mundhir
lines.role: tied himself to a pillar of the mosque in repentance after a mistake during the siege until Allah accepted his repentance.

head: p
jabir-ibn-abdullah
lines.role: narrated the hadith of the Throne shaking.

head: p
aishah-bint-abi-bakr
lines.role: described Sa'd's condition and the Prophet's grief.

head: p
umm-sad
lines.role: his mother, whom the Prophet ﷺ consoled.

stories.title: The Treaty of Hudaybiyah
paras: In 6 AH, the Prophet ﷺ set out with about 1,400 Companions for Umrah but was stopped at Hudaybiyah. He sent Uthman to negotiate, and when a rumour said Uthman was killed, the Companions pledged under a tree to stand firm. Quraysh then sent Suhayl ibn Amr, and a truce was signed with terms that seemed harsh to the Muslims. Allah called it "a clear victory" in Surah al-Fath, and within two years Islam spread more than ever before.

head: p
uthman-ibn-affan
lines.role: the envoy; the Prophet ﷺ pledged on his behalf with his own hand.

head: g
All who pledged under the tree (Bay'at al-Ridwan)
lines.role: Allah declared He was pleased with them (48:18).

head: p
salamah-ibn-al-akwa
lines.role: pledged three times at the Prophet's request.

head: p
ali-ibn-abi-talib
lines.role: wrote the treaty; the Prophet ﷺ himself erased "Messenger of Allah" when Ali would not.

head: p
umar-ibn-al-khattab
lines.role: questioned the terms in distress, later regretting it.

head: p
abu-bakr-al-siddiq
lines.role: calmed Umar with the same answer the Prophet ﷺ had given.

head: p
umm-salamah
lines.role: advised the Prophet ﷺ to shave his head first, after which all followed.

head: p
abu-jandal-ibn-suhayl
lines.role: escaped to the Muslims in chains and was returned under the treaty.

head: p
al-mughirah-ibn-shubah
lines.role: stood guard over the Prophet ﷺ with a sword.

head: p
abu-basir
lines.role: later escaped and formed a group whose pressure led Quraysh to drop the return clause.

head: p
suhayl-ibn-amr

head: p
urwah-ibn-masud-al-thaqafi
lines.role: envoy who reported the Companions' love for the Prophet ﷺ (accepted Islam later).

head: p
budayl-ibn-warqa-al-khuzai
lines.role: carried messages between the sides (accepted Islam later).

stories.title: The Conquest of Khaybar
paras: In 7 AH, the Muslims besieged the fortresses of Khaybar. After days of failed attempts, the Prophet ﷺ said, "Tomorrow I will give the flag to a man who loves Allah and His Messenger and whom Allah and His Messenger love." Everyone hoped for it, but he called Ali, who had sore eyes. The Prophet ﷺ applied his saliva, the eyes were healed, and the fortress fell.

head: p
ali-ibn-abi-talib
lines.role: given the flag; led the conquest of the fort.

head: p
sahl-ibn-sad
lines.role: narrated the hadith of the flag.

head: p
muhammad-ibn-maslamah
lines.role: killed the champion Marhab according to some reports (others name Ali).

head: p
amir-ibn-al-akwa
lines.role: recited poetry on the march; died when his own sword rebounded, and the Prophet ﷺ affirmed his double reward.

head: p
salamah-ibn-al-akwa
lines.role: his nephew, who narrated it.

head: p
safiyyah-bint-huyayy
lines.role: daughter of a Khaybar chief; married the Prophet ﷺ and became a Mother of the Believers.

head: p
jafar-ibn-abi-talib
lines.role: returned from Abyssinia; the Prophet ﷺ said, "I do not know which makes me happier, the conquest of Khaybar or the return of Ja'far."

head: p
abu-hurayrah
t
and
p
abu-musa-al-ashari
lines.role: arrived around this time and joined the Muslims.

head: p
bishr-ibn-al-bara-ibn-marur
lines.role: died after eating from the poisoned sheep offered to the Prophet ﷺ.

stories.title: The Battle of Mu'tah
paras: In 8 AH, 3,000 Muslims met a far larger Byzantine force. The Prophet ﷺ had named three commanders in turn: Zayd, then Ja'far, then Abdullah ibn Rawahah. All three were martyred. Khalid ibn al-Walid took the flag and withdrew the army skilfully. In Madinah, with tears in his eyes, the Prophet ﷺ announced each death before the news arrived, then said, "A sword from the swords of Allah took the flag."

head: p
zayd-ibn-harithah
lines.role: first commander; martyred.

head: p
jafar-ibn-abi-talib
lines.role: lost both hands holding the flag; given two wings in Paradise, hence "al-Tayyar."

head: p
abdullah-ibn-rawahah
lines.role: the poet; hesitated briefly, then advanced and was martyred.

head: p
thabit-ibn-aqram
lines.role: picked up the fallen flag and handed it to Khalid.

head: p
khalid-ibn-al-walid
lines.role: broke nine swords that day; named "Sword of Allah."

head: p
abdullah-ibn-umar
lines.role: counted over ninety wounds on Ja'far's front.

head: p
asma-bint-umays
lines.role: Ja'far's wife, to whom the Prophet ﷺ brought the news.

head: p
abdullah-ibn-jafar
lines.role: Ja'far's son, whom the Prophet ﷺ took in his care.

stories.title: The Conquest of Makkah
paras: When Quraysh's allies broke the Hudaybiyah truce, the Prophet ﷺ marched with 10,000 men in Ramadan of 8 AH. Makkah fell almost without fighting. He entered with his head bowed in humility, cleared 360 idols from around the Ka'bah reciting "Truth has come and falsehood has vanished" (17:81), and told his former persecutors, "No blame on you today. Go, you are free."

head: p
hatib-ibn-abi-baltaah
lines.role: secretly wrote to Quraysh to protect his family; forgiven as a man of Badr.

head: p
ali-ibn-abi-talib
t
p
al-zubayr-ibn-al-awwam

p
al-miqdad-ibn-al-aswad

head: p
umar-ibn-al-khattab
lines.role: wanted to punish Hatib; told Allah may have forgiven the people of Badr.

head: p
al-abbas-ibn-abd-al-muttalib
lines.role: brought Abu Sufyan to the Prophet ﷺ.

head: p
abu-sufyan-ibn-harb
lines.role: accepted Islam; "whoever enters Abu Sufyan's house is safe."

head: p
sad-ibn-ubadah
lines.role: said "Today is the day of slaughter"; the flag was given to his son Qays ibn Sa'd.

head: p
khalid-ibn-al-walid

abu-ubaydah-ibn-al-jarrah

head: p
bilal-ibn-rabah
lines.role: called the adhan from the roof of the Ka'bah.

head: p
uthman-ibn-talhah
lines.role: the Prophet ﷺ returned the key of the Ka'bah to him, forever with his family.

head: p
abu-quhafah
lines.role: Abu Bakr's elderly father; accepted Islam.

head: p
umm-hani-bint-abi-talib

head: p
hind-bint-utbah

stories.title: The Battle of Hunayn
paras: Weeks after the conquest, 12,000 Muslims met the Hawazin. Some were pleased by their numbers (9:25). Ambushed in a narrow valley, many fled, but the Prophet ﷺ rode forward saying, "I am the Prophet, no lie; I am the son of Abd al-Muttalib." Al-Abbas called the Companions back, and they won. When the spoils went to new Muslims of Quraysh, some Ansar felt hurt, and the Prophet ﷺ told them, "Are you not pleased that people go home with sheep and camels, and you go home with the Messenger of Allah?" They wept until their beards were wet.

head: p
al-abbas-ibn-abd-al-muttalib
lines.role: called out, "O people of the tree of Ridwan!"

head: p
abu-sufyan-ibn-al-harith
lines.role: the Prophet's cousin; held the reins of his mule.

head: p

p

head: p
ayman-ibn-umm-ayman
lines.role: stood firm and was martyred.

head: p
umm-sulaym-bint-milhan
lines.role: carried a dagger to defend herself and the Prophet ﷺ.

head: p
al-bara-ibn-azib
lines.role: narrated the Prophet's words during the retreat.

head: p
sad-ibn-ubadah
lines.role: told the Prophet ﷺ of the Ansar's feelings and gathered them.

head: p
abu-said-al-khudri
lines.role: narrated the speech to the Ansar.

head: p
al-shayma-bint-al-harith
lines.role: his foster sister from Halimah, brought as a captive; he spread his cloak for her.

head: p
malik-ibn-awf-al-nasri
lines.role: commander of Hawazin (accepted Islam later).

stories.title: The Expedition of Tabuk
paras: In 9 AH, in severe heat and poverty, the Prophet ﷺ called for an expedition to Tabuk against Byzantium, known as the "army of hardship." Companions gave all they could. Uthman equipped a large part of the army, and the Prophet ﷺ said, "Nothing Uthman does after today will harm him." The army waited twenty days at Tabuk, no battle took place, and the tribes of the north made treaties.

head: p
uthman-ibn-affan
lines.role: gave hundreds of camels and 1,000 dinars.

head: p
abu-bakr-al-siddiq
lines.role: gave all his wealth, leaving "Allah and His Messenger" for his family.

head: p
umar-ibn-al-khattab
lines.role: gave half his wealth, hoping to surpass Abu Bakr.

head: p
abd-al-rahman-ibn-awf
lines.role: gave a large sum.

head: p
abu-aqil-al-ansari
lines.role: gave a small measure of dates earned by night labour; mocked by hypocrites, honoured by Allah (9:79).

head: g
Al-Bakka'un (the weepers)
lines.role: poor Companions with no mounts who wept at being left behind (9:92).

head: p
ali-ibn-abi-talib
lines.role: left in charge of the household: "Are you not pleased to be to me as Harun was to Musa?"

head: p
abu-khaythamah
lines.role: stayed at first, then rode alone to catch up.

head: p
abu-dharr-al-ghifari
lines.role: walked when his camel failed; "he walks alone, will die alone, and be raised alone."

head: p
kab-ibn-malik

stories.title: Ka'b ibn Malik and the Three Who Stayed Behind
paras: Ka'b had no excuse for missing Tabuk and refused to invent one. The Prophet ﷺ ordered the Muslims not to speak to him or his two companions for fifty days. The king of Ghassan wrote inviting him over; Ka'b threw the letter into an oven. On the fiftieth morning, Allah revealed their forgiveness (9:118), and a man ran up the mountain shouting the good news.

head: p
kab-ibn-malik
lines.role: told the truth; narrated the whole story.

head: p
murarah-ibn-al-rabi
t
and
p
hilal-ibn-umayyah
lines.role: the two other men of Badr who stayed behind.

head: p
abu-qatadah-al-ansari
lines.role: Ka'b's cousin and closest friend, who would not reply to him.

head: p
talhah-ibn-ubaydillah
lines.role: rose and shook Ka'b's hand in the mosque; Ka'b never forgot it.

head: g
Hilal's wife
lines.role: allowed to keep serving her elderly husband.

head: p
abdullah-ibn-kab
lines.role: Ka'b's son, who narrated the story from him.

head: p
abu-bakr-al-siddiq
lines.role: announced the good news from the mountain, according to some reports.

stories.title: Uthman and the Well of Rumah
paras: When the Muslims reached Madinah, sweet water was scarce, and the well of Rumah belonged to a man who sold its water at a high price. The Prophet ﷺ said, "Whoever buys the well of Rumah and makes it free for the Muslims will have a better one in Paradise." Uthman bought it, first half then all, and made it a free endowment for everyone.

head: p
uthman-ibn-affan
lines.role: bought the well; reminded the people of it during the siege of his house years later.

head: g
The Muslims of Madinah
lines.role: who drank from it freely.

stories.title: The Slander Against Aishah (al-Ifk)
paras: Returning from an expedition, Aishah left the camp to search for a lost necklace, and the army departed without her. Safwan ibn al-Mu'attal found her and brought her back, leading the camel on foot. Hypocrites spread a lie about her, and for a month Madinah was troubled. Then Allah revealed ten verses of Surah al-Nur declaring her innocence.

head: p
aishah-bint-abi-bakr
lines.role: declared innocent by revelation; narrated the full account.

head: p
safwan-ibn-al-muattal
lines.role: the Companion who found her; also cleared.

head: p
abu-bakr-al-siddiq
t
and
p
umm-ruman
lines.role: her parents, who suffered with her.

head: p
barirah
lines.role: her servant, who testified she knew only good of her.

head: p
zaynab-bint-jahsh
lines.role: co-wife who, when asked, protected Aishah's honour.

head: p
ali-ibn-abi-talib
t
and
p
usamah-ibn-zayd
lines.role: consulted by the Prophet ﷺ.

head: p
umm-mistah
lines.role: told Aishah of the rumours.

head: p
mistah-ibn-uthathah
t
p
hassan-ibn-thabit
t
and
p
hamnah-bint-jahsh
lines.role: repeated the slander and repented; Abu Bakr resumed supporting Mistah after verse 24:22.

head: p
sad-ibn-muadh
t
and
p
sad-ibn-ubadah
lines.role: argued in the mosque over how to deal with the slanderers.

stories.title: Zayd ibn Harithah Chooses the Prophet ﷺ
paras: Zayd was kidnapped as a child and sold in Makkah; Khadijah gave him to the Prophet ﷺ before prophethood. Years later his father and uncle found him and came to buy his freedom. The Prophet ﷺ let Zayd choose freely. Zayd chose to stay, saying he would choose no one over him. The Prophet ﷺ then declared him his son before Quraysh.

head: p
zayd-ibn-harithah
lines.role: the only Companion named in the Qur'an (33:37).

head: p
khadijah-bint-khuwaylid
lines.role: gave Zayd to the Prophet ﷺ.

head: p
usamah-ibn-zayd
lines.role: his son, "the beloved son of the beloved."

head: p
umm-ayman
lines.role: Zayd's later wife and Usamah's mother.

stories.title: Abu Hurayrah and the Cup of Milk
paras: Abu Hurayrah lived in the mosque with the poor of al-Suffah. One day, faint with hunger, he sat on the road hoping someone would invite him. The Prophet ﷺ saw his face, brought him home and sent him to call all the people of al-Suffah to share a single cup of milk. Abu Hurayrah served everyone first, then the Prophet ﷺ told him, "Drink," again and again, until he said, "I can drink no more." Abu Hurayrah also wept that his mother refused Islam. The Prophet ﷺ prayed for her, and he returned home to find her accepting Islam.

head: p
abu-hurayrah
lines.role: the narrator; later the most prolific narrator of hadith.

head: p
umaymah-bint-subayh
lines.role: his mother, who accepted Islam through the Prophet's prayer.

head: g
Ahl al-Suffah
lines.role: the poor Companions of the mosque who shared the cup.

head: p
abu-bakr-al-siddiq
t
and
p
umar-ibn-al-khattab
lines.role: passed by first; Abu Hurayrah asked them about a verse hoping for food.

stories.title: Abu Talhah and Umm Sulaym: Generosity and Patience
paras: A hungry guest came to the Prophet ﷺ, and Abu Talhah took him home with only enough food for their children. Umm Sulaym put the children to sleep and dimmed the lamp so the guest would not see they were not eating. In the morning, the Prophet ﷺ said Allah had admired their deed, and verse 59:9 was revealed. When their young son later died, Umm Sulaym prepared her husband's meal before gently telling him, and the Prophet ﷺ prayed for blessing on their night. They were given a son, Abdullah, whose children all memorised the Qur'an.

head: p
abu-talhah-al-ansari
lines.role: the host.

head: p
umm-sulaym-bint-milhan
lines.role: his wife; famous for her wisdom and patience. Her mahr was Abu Talhah's Islam.

head: p
abu-umayr
lines.role: their young son who died; the Prophet ﷺ used to tease him about his pet bird.

head: p
abdullah-ibn-abi-talhah
lines.role: the son born after.

head: p
anas-ibn-malik
lines.role: Umm Sulaym's son, the narrator.

head: p
abu-hurayrah
lines.role: narrated the hadith of the guest.

stories.title: Sawad ibn Ghaziyyah at Badr
paras: As the Prophet ﷺ straightened the ranks at Badr with an arrow, he poked Sawad in the stomach. Sawad said, "You have hurt me; let me take retribution." The Prophet ﷺ uncovered his stomach. Sawad embraced him and kissed it, saying, "I wanted my last contact in this world to be my skin touching yours." The Prophet ﷺ prayed for him.

head: p
sawad-ibn-ghaziyyah
lines.role: the Companion of the ranks.

head: g
The army of Badr
lines.role: witnessed it as the ranks were straightened.

stories.title: Julaybib
paras: Julaybib was a poor man of humble appearance with no family. The Prophet ﷺ himself asked an Ansari family for their daughter's hand on his behalf. The parents hesitated, but the daughter said, "Will you reject the Messenger's request? Send me to him." Soon after, Julaybib was martyred in battle having killed seven. The Prophet ﷺ searched for him, laid him on his own arms, and said, "He is from me and I am from him."

head: p
julaybib
lines.role: the martyr.

head: g
His Ansari wife and her parents
lines.role: she is unnamed in the Sahih narration; the Prophet ﷺ prayed for abundant blessing on her.

head: p
abu-barzah-al-aslami
lines.role: narrated the account in Sahih Muslim.

stories.title: Mu'adh ibn Jabal Sent to Yemen
paras: When sending Mu'adh to Yemen, the Prophet ﷺ asked how he would judge. Mu'adh said by the Book of Allah, then the Sunnah, then by his own reasoning. The Prophet ﷺ praised Allah. Another time he took Mu'adh's hand and said, "O Mu'adh, by Allah, I love you," and taught him to say after every prayer, "O Allah, help me to remember You, thank You and worship You well." Walking beside Mu'adh's mount as he left, he told him he might not see him again. Mu'adh wept.

head: p
muadh-ibn-jabal
lines.role: the scholar of halal and haram.

head: p
abu-musa-al-ashari
lines.role: sent to Yemen at the same time: "Make things easy, not difficult."

stories.title: Abdullah ibn Umm Maktum and Surah Abasa
paras: The Prophet ﷺ was inviting Quraysh leaders when the blind Companion Ibn Umm Maktum came asking to be taught. The Prophet ﷺ frowned and turned away, hoping to win the leaders. Allah revealed "He frowned and turned away" (80:1). Afterwards the Prophet ﷺ honoured him, saying, "Welcome to the one about whom my Lord reproached me," and made him deputy in Madinah many times.

head: p
abdullah-ibn-umm-maktum
lines.role: the blind Companion; mu'adhdhin and deputy governor of Madinah.

head: p
aishah-bint-abi-bakr
lines.role: narrated the occasion of revelation.

stories.title: Usamah's Intercession and Justice for All
paras: A woman of the noble Makhzum clan committed theft. Quraysh, worried for their status, asked Usamah, the Prophet's beloved, to intercede. The Prophet ﷺ said, "Do you intercede regarding a limit set by Allah?" He stood and declared that earlier nations were destroyed because they spared the noble and punished the weak, adding, "If Fatimah the daughter of Muhammad stole, I would cut her hand."

head: p
usamah-ibn-zayd
lines.role: the intercessor, who asked forgiveness.

head: p
fatimah-bint-al-aswad-al-makhzumiyyah
lines.role: the woman; she repented and later lived righteously.

head: p
aishah-bint-abi-bakr
lines.role: narrated the hadith and said the woman's repentance was sincere.

head: p
fatimah-bint-muhammad
lines.role: named as the example in his words.

stories.title: Abu Dharr Accepts Islam
paras: Hearing of a prophet in Makkah, Abu Dharr of Ghifar sent his brother, then went himself. He sat in the mosque for days, afraid to ask. Ali noticed the stranger and quietly led him to the Prophet ﷺ, where he accepted Islam. Abu Dharr then shouted the testimony of faith at the Ka'bah and was beaten until al-Abbas warned Quraysh that Ghifar lay on their trade route. He returned home, and half his tribe accepted Islam.

stories.title: Al-Tufayl ibn Amr al-Dawsi
paras: Al-Tufayl, a poet and chief of Daws, was warned by Quraysh not to listen to the Prophet ﷺ, so he stuffed cotton in his ears. Then he thought, "I am an intelligent man; I can tell good from bad." He listened, accepted Islam, and asked for a sign. A light shone on his whip as he returned. When his tribe was slow to respond, the Prophet ﷺ prayed, "O Allah, guide Daws," and later eighty families came to Madinah.

stories.title: Ikrimah ibn Abi Jahl's Return
paras: After the conquest of Makkah, Ikrimah, son of the Prophet's fiercest enemy, fled to Yemen. His wife Umm Hakim accepted Islam and secured a pardon for him. When he arrived, the Prophet ﷺ stood and greeted him warmly, and told his Companions not to insult Ikrimah's father in front of him, for insulting the dead hurts the living. Ikrimah became a devoted Muslim and was martyred at Yarmuk.

stories.title: Wahshi, the Killer of Hamzah
paras: Wahshi, an Abyssinian slave, killed Hamzah at Uhud in return for his freedom. After the conquest of Makkah he feared for his life, then learned the Prophet ﷺ did not kill those who came to Islam. He came and accepted Islam. The Prophet ﷺ forgave him but asked, "Can you keep your face away from me?" Years later, Wahshi killed the false prophet Musaylimah at Yamamah with the same spear.

stories.title: Thumamah ibn Uthal
paras: Thumamah, a chief of Yamamah, was captured by a Muslim cavalry unit and tied to a pillar of the mosque. For three days the Prophet ﷺ asked him how he was and treated him kindly, then freed him without ransom. Thumamah bathed, returned and accepted Islam, saying, "No face on earth was more hateful to me than yours; now it is the most beloved." He then cut off grain from Yamamah to Makkah until Quraysh begged the Prophet ﷺ to intervene.

stories.title: The Delegation of Najran and the Mubahalah
paras: A Christian delegation from Najran came to discuss Isa (Jesus). When they would not accept the Qur'an's teaching, Allah commanded the Prophet ﷺ to invite them to a mutual invocation of Allah's curse on the liars (3:61). He came out with Ali, Fatimah, Hasan and Husayn. The delegation declined and made a peace treaty instead. They asked for a trustworthy man, and he sent Abu Ubaydah, "the trustworthy one of this Ummah."

stories.title: Ali and Fatimah: Marriage and the Gift of Tasbih
paras: Ali married Fatimah with a simple mahr from the sale of his armour. Their home was humble. Fatimah's hands were blistered from the grinding stone, and Ali's chest ached from drawing water, so they asked the Prophet ﷺ for a servant from the captives. He came to them at night and said, "Shall I tell you something better than a servant? When you go to bed, say SubhanAllah 33 times, Alhamdulillah 33 times and Allahu Akbar 34 times." Ali said he never left it afterwards.

stories.title: The Farewell Pilgrimage
paras: In 10 AH, the Prophet ﷺ made his only Hajj with over 100,000 people. At Arafah he gave his great sermon: lives, wealth and honour are sacred; usury and blood feuds of ignorance are abolished; treat women well; hold to the Book of Allah. He asked, "Have I conveyed?" and they said, "Yes," and he raised his finger to the sky: "O Allah, bear witness." Then the verse was revealed: "This day I have perfected your religion for you" (5:3).

stories.title: The Final Illness and Passing of the Prophet ﷺ
paras: In Rabi' al-Awwal of 11 AH, the Prophet ﷺ fell ill and asked to be nursed in Aishah's house. When he could no longer lead the prayer, he said, "Tell Abu Bakr to lead the people." On his last morning he lifted the curtain and smiled at the rows behind Abu Bakr. He died with his head on Aishah's chest, saying, "With the highest companion." When Umar refused to believe it, Abu Bakr recited, "Muhammad is but a messenger; messengers have passed away before him" (3:144), and said, "Whoever worshipped Muhammad, Muhammad has died; whoever worshipped Allah, Allah is alive and never dies."
